Article Title: Dhruv Jurel at a crossroads in Galle: Time to turn promise into permanence
Article Text:
India's Dhruv Jurel gets bowled by Afghanistan's Mohammad Saleem on day two of a Test cricket match between India and Afghanistan, in Mullanpur. (PTI)

TimesofIndia.com in Galle:

**EDS: THIRD PARTY IMAGE** In this image received on June 28, 2026, India's captain Dhruv Jurel plays a shot on day four of the unofficial Test series between India A and Sri Lanka A in the Tri-Nation A Series, in Galle, Sri Lanka. (SLC via PTI Photo)(PTI06_28_2026_000484B) *** Local Caption ***

Dhruv Jurel

Dhruv Jurel

At the Nondescripts Cricket Club (NCC) Ground in Colombo, Dhruv Jurel was sitting by himself when a chirpy Sarfaraz Khan , who had joined the team just hours earlier, walked up to greet him. The duo share a special history, having made their Test debuts together against England in Rajkot two years ago. However, their careers have taken different turns since then. While Sarfaraz has struggled for regular opportunities, Jurel has established himself as a regular in the Test squad and was also picked as a back-up wicketkeeper-batter for India’s limited-overs teams.Despite contrasting game time and backing, Jurel is yet to cement his spot in the playing XI, even when the management has backed him as a specialist batter in the presence of Rishabh Pant, India's first-choice wicketkeeper in Tests. Jurel's career has so far followed a very frustrating pattern: he has had solid outings in shadow and preparatory fixtures but has failed to carry that form into the international arena.Before the 2024 Border-Gavaskar Trophy, Jurel was sent early to prepare with the India A team, where he scored 80 and 68 in two outings at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG). He played only one game in the series, at Perth, scoring 11 and 1.A few months later, he turned up for India A against England Lions before the Anderson-Tendulkar Test series. Jurel scored 94 and 53 not out at Canterbury. He was on the bench for four Tests in England before replacing the injured Rishabh Pant for a crucial fixture at The Oval. His scores of 19 and 34 in the two innings brought his long summer to a disappointing end.Next up was the home season, featuring four fixtures against the West Indies and South Africa. India had identified a need for a right-hander in the mix and, with the management unwilling to go back to Karun Nair, Jurel became the favourite to get more game time as a specialist batter. India A hosted Australia A for two fixtures and, in both games, Dhruv made a strong case for himself. Scores of 1, 56 and 140 were enough to earn the faith of the men who matter for the West Indies and South Africa Tests.Jurel played all four games, scoring his maiden Test hundred against the West Indies in Ahmedabad, but managed only 29 runs in four innings against South Africa. It is understood that the think tank was not at all pleased with his outings in Kolkata and Guwahati and even reminded him that he needed to perform much better to remain relevant as a pure batter. Then came the white-ball fixtures, the IPL and a one-off Test against Afghanistan, where the 25-year-old would have felt gutted to return with only 19 runs to his name.The low scores and the manner in which he has thrown his wickets away have surprised the management.In the first Test against South Africa at the Eden Gardens, off-spinner Simon Harmer dismissed him on both occasions. In the first innings, Jurel chipped a return catch, while in the second essay, he pulled a rank hop delivery straight to the throat of the lone man patrolling at deep midwicket.In the first innings of the second Test in Guwahati, Jurel failed with a pull shot again, this time against left-arm quick Marco Jansen. Jurel went for an extravagant pull shot and ended up popping an easy catch to mid-on.His misery followed him to New Chandigarh during the one-off Test against Afghanistan as well. It was brain fade, to say the least, from the batter. Jurel left a ball thinking it would bounce over the wicket, but instead it nipped back and kissed the top of off stump.However, the build-up to the two Tests in Sri Lanka was again a familiar one for Jurel. He toured with the India A team last month and had scores of 14, 141* and 53 in Galle. The warm-up outings in Colombo weren't ideal, nor was his hit in the match simulation. In the two outings at the NCC, Jurel managed 1 and 17. The second-innings dismissal will again raise questions over his judgement.The Galle Test might prove to be his chance to shake off his string of poor scores in Test cricket and repay the faith that the selectors and team management have shown in him over the last two years. Jurel had played only 15 first-class matches, with a highest score of 249 against a weak Nagaland side. But there was something about him that caught the eye of the Indian selection panel, headed by Ajit Agarkar, and he received his maiden call-up. Rishabh Pant was still recovering from a horrific car accident, KS Bharat played the first two Tests against England, and then, in Rajkot, Jurel got his chance."Great work ethic. Very sincere guy. Nice kid. Very nice to speak to. Understands his cricket. Very intelligent as far as his game is concerned," former India batting coach Vikram Rathour told TimesofIndia.com in October last year.“Rajkot was the first time I saw him play. And then in Ranchi, he played a fantastic knock, that partnership with Kuldeep (Yadav) was phenomenal. In that series, a couple of knocks he played were incredible. The chase in Ranchi is something I will always remember. It was difficult conditions, we were under pressure, and the series was on the line,” Rathour said, praising Jurel for his gutsy 90 in the Ranchi Test against England.Cut to the present, the 25-year-old now has two net sessions to regain his touch and confidence and ensure the management that he is the right choice for No. 6 in India's Test set-up. With Sarfaraz Khan back in the mix, the onus will be on Jurel to cement his spot. However, his place, at least for the Galle Test, seems safe, but the presence of Sarfaraz certainly puts more options on the table.The youngster is widely liked in the dressing room for his impeccable work ethic. He is one of the hardest workers in the room, and the effort he puts into his preparations hasn't gone unnoticed. However, after more than two years with the Test team, performance, not effort, needs to speak. And starting August 15, it will not only be a trial by spin for the Indian cricket team but also a baptism of fire for Dhruv, provided he retains his spot, to make the position his own for the foreseeable future.
Article Summary: Dhruv Jurel is yet to cement his spot in the playing XI, even when the management has backed him as a specialist batter. The 25-year-old was sent early to prepare with the India A team, where he scored 80 and 68 in two outings at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. He played only one game in the series, at Perth, scoring 11 and 1.

Article Title: Hardik Pandya's Gujarat Titans trade collapses over captaincy demand
Article Text:
Mumbai Indians Hardik Pandya (ANI Photo)

Hardik’s comeback likely vs Afg

Mumbai: Hardik Pandya ’s search for a way out of Mumbai Indians has hit another roadblock. TOI has learnt that the India allrounder explored a return to Gujarat Titans, the franchise he led to the IPL title in 2022 and the final in 2023, but talks broke down after he insisted on being reinstated as captain.GT were open to bringing back the 32-year-old, but unwilling to replace Shubman Gill , now India’s Test and ODI captain. “Which team wouldn’t want Hardik ? But his captaincy condition killed the deal,” a source said.Pandya enjoyed the best phase of his IPL career at Gujarat, where he revived his international career and established himself as a leader. However, sources indicated that while GT valued his experience, they expected him to return as a senior player rather than captain.His future at MI remains uncertain after another disappointing season. Mumbai finished ninth in IPL 2026, extending their title drought to six years. Hardik’s own returns were modest: 206 runs at 22.88 and four wickets in 10 matches, with back spasms restricting him to only 10 appearances.Since replacing Rohit Sharma as MI skipper in 2024, Pandya has endured a turbulent spell. MI finished last that season, recovered to reach the playoffs in 2025 before slipping back to ninth this year.The move from Rohit to Hardik also triggered a hostile reaction from sections of the franchise’s fan base.With Ajinkya Rahane retired and Rishabh Pant stepping down as LSG captain after successive poor campaigns, Kolkata Knight Riders and Lucknow Super Giants could emerge as possible destinations if Pandya remains keen on a leadership role.Adding to the uncertainty, MI batting coach Kieron Pollard had stopped short of guaranteeing Hardik’s continuation as captain after the franchise endured another horror season in May.“Yes, it might not have gone as well as he would have wanted, what we would have wanted, but I wouldn’t question anything at this time. Twelve months ago, we finished third. Now again, we finished ninth. Those are the inconsistencies we will have to address. We will sit and talk, lick our wounds and hopefully come back stronger in 12 months’ time. He was trying. We all were trying. We tried each and everything to give the best opportunity for him to lead the franchise and do well,” Pollard had replied when quizzed about Hardik’s leadership at MI.For now, Pandya’s focus is on returning to full fitness. He has been training at BCCI’s Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, bowling up to 10 overs and batting extensively in the nets. Sources said he is expected to be available for India’s home T20I series against Afghanistan, beginning in New Delhi on Sept 13.
Article Summary: Hardik Pandya explored a return to Gujarat Titans, the franchise he led to the IPL title in 2022 and the final in 2023. Talks broke down after he insisted on being reinstated as captain. GT were open to bringing back the 32-year-old, but unwilling to replace Shubman Gill, now India's Test and ODI captain.

Article Title: 'We have the upper hand': Sri Lanka captain's warning to India ahead of Galle Test
Article Text:
Sri Lankan batsman Dhananjaya de Silva (AP/PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: The first battle of the upcoming India-Sri Lanka Test series may begin long before a ball turns sharply off the Galle surface. It may begin in the minds of the batters.Sri Lanka know what Galle — the venue for the first Test — can become. They know how quickly a pitch that looks inviting on the first morning can begin asking different questions by the third day. They know what happens when the ball starts gripping, when the rough comes into play and when a batter who has spent two days playing straight suddenly has to decide whether to attack, defend or simply survive.And they know India have had their own recent troubles against spin, losing home Test series to New Zealand and South Africa in the last two years. Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva does not believe India’s defeats on turning pitches mean they have forgotten how to bat against spin. If anything, he expects a wounded opponent.“Well, India did lose two series (against New Zealand and South Africa) in India on turning wickets, but it’s not that they have forgotten how to play on turning wickets. They’ll surely be itching to make a comeback,” De Silva told TOI ahead of the first Test in Galle on Saturday.Sri Lanka’s strategy will be to drag India deep into the Test, let the surface age, allow the spinners to dictate the questions and see who has the answers.“International cricket is not easy. If we can take the games to the fourth and fifth day, we will have a greater chance to beat them,” De Silva said. “I hope we make it as hard as possible for them and they are under the pump during the series.”The hosts are not expecting a pitch that turns square from the first hour. The weather has intervened. It has been raining in Sri Lanka, and De Silva expects conditions to remain relatively humid rather than dry. His preference is for a sporting surface — one that rewards batters early before gradually bringing the spinners into the contest.“Normally, we get spinning wickets in Sri Lanka. But currently, it’s raining here and weather conditions are not going to be dry,” he said.“We have a strong batting lineup as well, so I feel pitches will be sporting — helping batters in the first 2-3 days and then start turning. Spinners are going to be our primary line of attack. But, that said, we’ve some quality seamers in our team who can change the game,” he added.The Lankan captain believes the hardest part of batting in these conditions is not necessarily negotiating the first spell of spin. It is knowing what to do when the surface begins to change.“The difference is that it’s quite hard to get runs over here and the batters really need to dig in and show temperament to score sizeable number of runs,” De Silva said.That, he feels, is where Sri Lanka possess an advantage.“We know how to approach our innings. We know when it’s going to start turning. Several batters become clueless when it turns and don’t know how to go about a knock in these conditions.”There is another reason the spin battle could become the defining thread of the series — Lankan left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya, who has made Galle his territory.“Stats-wise, we have the upper hand. Prabath has played more matches than any other guys in the two teams, especially in Galle,” De Silva said. “He has had the upper hand over many touring batting lineups over the years. Plus-one to Sri Lanka, I would say.”India, of course, are not short of players who know how to win in difficult conditions. However, some key names are missing. De Silva, of course, is not allowing any sense of complacency to seep in.“Even if India are missing some of their key players, I’m not going to take them lightly. They have several match-winners in their team,” he said.Jasprit Bumrah’s absence, though, stands out.“He (Bumrah) will be a big loss for India,” De Silva said. “But we’ve done our homework for others and we’re well prepared for them.”Sri Lanka arrive with confidence from their recent tour of the West Indies, where their batters scored hundreds, their pacers produced five-wicket hauls and Jayasuriya performed strongly.“In the second Test, we ran West Indies very close and had them on the backfoot,” De Silva said. “That kind of performance boosts our confidence.”According to De Silva, India’s biggest threat during the series is likely to be opening batter KL Rahul.“I would say experience-wise KL Rahul would be the biggest threat for us. He has done well all around the world and he has played a few matches in Sri Lanka as well. Last time (in 2017), I think he played in our conditions and knows it pretty well.”(Watch the India-SL Test series live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV)
Article Summary: Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva believes India have forgotten how to bat on turning wickets. Sri Lanka's strategy will be to drag India deep into the Test, let the surface age and allow the spinners to dictate the questions. De Silva expects conditions to remain relatively humid rather than dry.

Article Title: Ministry suspends TTFI over governance, selection issues
Article Text:
Sports Ministry suspends recognition of Table Tennis Federation of India over governance issues

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: Noting that the internal conflict and power struggle in the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) has the potential to “prejudice the interests of athletes and other stakeholders as well as blemish the country’s image in the international sports arena”, the sports ministry on Wednesday suspended recognition of the national federation and asked the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) to form an ad hoc committee to run the sport.The decision, coming weeks ahead of the Asian Games in Japan, is unlikely to directly affect India’s participation, with the team selection process already completed and the IOA’s interim arrangement set to oversee the contingent. However, during the suspension, TTFI will not be entitled to financial assistance, official patronage or other benefits accruing from recognition as an NSF.The ministry cited repeated non-compliance with its directions, deficiencies in institutional functioning and continuing governance concerns. It flagged the appointment of Mahinder Pal Singh as CEO at an AGM, in contravention of ministry directives, and the process adopted to constitute the grievance/dispute redressal committee.The ministry was particularly critical of TTFI’s selection policy, saying it violated its March 2025 guidelines. “The selection policy raises concerns about fairness in the selection criteria and is also disadvantageous and puts restriction on some meritorious athletes who are regularly participating at the international circuit and having better world rankings,” the suspension order read, a copy of which is with TOI.It added that the policy did not address selection criteria for mega events such as the Olympics or Asian Games, despite their differing qualification pathways, and provided no mechanism for redressal of athletes’ selection grievances.The ministry also pointed to the continuing differences between president Meghna Ahlawat and secretary general Kamlesh Mehta, saying allegations and counter-allegations had adversely affected decision-making and undermined confidence in TTFI’s governance.The suspension follows a show-cause notice issued to TTFI in June, with the ministry terming its response unsatisfactory. The IOA has been asked to consult the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF) and constitute an interim mechanism until a compliant governance structure is restored.The federation had also come under scrutiny after star player Manika Batra was left out of the Asian Games squad, following which she alleged that the federation’s selection process was ambiguous and unfair.
Article Summary: Sports Ministry suspends recognition of Table Tennis Federation of India over governance issues. Decision unlikely to directly affect India’s participation in the Asian Games. TTFI will not be entitled to financial assistance, official patronage or other benefits accruing from recognition as an NSF.

Article Title: From dried village ponds to Oregon’s fields, Ashish Yadav’s silver forged in hardship
Article Text:
Ashish Yadav wins javelin silver at World U20 Championships

TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

While most of India waits for rains, Ashish Yadav would wait for it to stop.Because, during monsoons the village pond would swell up and the 19-year-old would then begin the long wait for summer when the pond would dry up and he would obtain his ‘training ground’.“Hurling the wooden pole in the village pond was exciting,” the Mirzapur village resident tells. In summers, the dried pond bed — benthic zone, for the more scientifically inclined — would become an ideal place to test his skills. In the rainy season, young Ashish searched for an empty field since the Uttar Pradesh village had no proper ground to practise. Dry ponds became his training ground, and a wooden pole served as a javelin.Last week, in Eugene, Oregon, a far cry from the makeshift practice ‘grounds’ of his village, all those hardships bore fruit with Yadav’s 74.09m effort fetching him silver in the men’s javelin at the U20 World Athletics Championships. The effort ended India’s 10-year wait for a medal since Neeraj Chopra ’s historic gold in 2016 at Bydgoszcz, which had crowned him the country’s first world U20 champion.“It was my first global competition and I emerged victorious.This silver medal is like gold for me,” said Yadav, who secured the medal with his third attempt. South Africa’s Jan-Hendrik Heymans won gold with 80.50m, while Dominica’s Addison James took bronze with 73.89m.Yadav, along with other two medal winners, Basant Kumar Meghwal (men’s high jump) and Shahnavaz Khan (men’s long jump), were felicitated by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) at its headquarters here on Wednesday.“This medal has also provided me with a healing touch. I had finished fourth at the Asian U20 meet in Hong Kong and was disappointed. I was hurting from inside. I was hungrier for a medal than my rivals,” he added.The youngster’s love for javelin began when his uncle Dharamraj Yadav, a former national-level discus thrower, urged him to find something productive in his life. “I used to play with village children and didn’t focus on classes and school. That was the time I started javelin throw,” he recalled. Those village contests sharpened his competitive spirit. “Who will throw the furthest was the mantra of each of the students,” he said.Money was tight, and Yadav, the second son of a small farmer, grew up in a family of modest means. His father sold milk at home, while his elder brother still works on farms, and his younger brother is in school. “It was tough growing up with limited means of income.But my father and entire family supported me and encouraged me to pursue sports.”A major change came in 2025, when Yadav shifted to the SAI centre in Hisar. Structured training, equipment, nutrition and injury management transformed his approach. “I learned a new throwing technique. I also learned injury management. There was a proper diet.”Yadav’s personal best is 74.49m, which he achieved at the Indian Open Throws competition in Patiala earlier this year. Now, he has bigger ambitions -- to breach the 80m-mark. “I have to stay healthy to achieve new goals in the coming months and not rest on my laurels. My goal is to work hard and climb up the ladder step by step. I want to get to the 80m,” he said.
Article Summary: Ashish Yadav won silver in the men's javelin at the U20 World Athletics Championships. His effort ended India’s 10-year wait for a medal since Neeraj Chopra ’s historic gold in 2016 at Bydgoszcz, which had crowned him the country's first world U20 champion. Yadav, along with other two medal winners, Basant Kumar Meghwal and Shahnavaz Khan, were felicitated by the Athletics Federation of India.

Article Title: Salima Tete to Deepika Sehrawat: Five players India will rely on at Hockey World Cup
Article Text:
India’s World Cup X-factor: Five players who could change the game

Salima Tete

When the Indian women’s hockey team walks out against China at Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, they will be competing in the World Cup for the ninth time, and it will be their third consecutive appearance in the tournament. India finished eighth in 2018 and ninth in 2022, but their best-ever finish came at the inaugural World Cup in 1974, when they finished fourth.To match or better that performance this Indian team will have to play out of its skin. Ranked ninth in the world, India had to fight hard to reach the tournament. After a disappointing last year, the team has shown a marked improvement in 2026 under the returning Sjoerd Marijne, with its best performance coming at the Nations Cup, where India lifted the title after beating hosts New Zealand in the final.If India are to carry that momentum into the World Cup, these five players will have a major role to play:The India skipper didn’t have the best of years in 2025, with the goals drying up and the pressure of captaincy seemingly weighing on her. She struggled to play her natural game. But things have certainly improved this year, and if India are to make it to the next round, Tete will have to play a pivotal role in the centre of the park.A world-class midfielder who has evolved into a goal-scoring machine, Navneet can hurt opponents from open play as well as penalty corners. Add to that her leadership qualities, which were evident when she led SG Pipers to victory in the women’s HIL earlier this year, and India have a player capable of making a difference at both ends of the pitch.This will be her third World Cup, and under coach Marijne, the Mizoram forward has reinvented herself. Operating just behind the forward line, the diminutive 26-year-old has become an important link in India’s attacking play, helping create chances and making clever runs into the circle. It was on full display during Nations Cup, where she also produced a standout performance in the final and was named Player of the Match.After struggling with injuries for months, the drag-flick specialist returned to the squad and made her presence felt, scoring six goals from penalty corners during the Nations Cup. It was a tremendous showing from the youngster as she showcased her full repertoire, from finding the corners to beating goalkeepers through their legs. Her drag-flicking was one of the highlights of India’s title-winning campaign and played a key role in their return to the Pro League.The youngster’s pace down the right flank has troubled many a team, and once she gets going, there is little opponents can do to contain her. She has also gained valuable experience playing alongside some of the best players in the world, and India will be hoping the 19-year-old can use that exposure to play a major role in their World Cup campaign.
Article Summary: India will be competing in the World Cup for the ninth time in 2026. It will be their third consecutive appearance in the tournament. India finished eighth in 2018 and ninth in 2022, but their best-ever finish came at the inaugural World Cup in 1974.

Article Title: FIH Hockey World Cup 2026: India's debutants ready to turn dreams into reality
Article Text:
Lalthantluangi and Shilpi Dabas

Ishika ready to repay family's faith

Lalthantluangi: 'The real work starts now'

Sakshi ready for first World Cup

Dabas' long wait finally ends

Toppo ready to use her speed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ready for the biggest stage

NEW DELHI: For some of India's young women's hockey players, the journey to the World Cup has been filled with challenges, setbacks and long waits.Now, Ishika, Lalthantluangi, Sakshi Rana, Shilpi Dabas and Sunelita Toppo are ready to make the most of their opportunity on hockey's biggest stage.For the five debutants, making the World Cup squad is the result of years of hard work, sacrifice and patience. They will now look to turn that journey into strong performances for India.For 21-year-old Ishika, playing in the World Cup is a dream that has finally come true.“Representing India at the biggest stage is every player’s dream. It really feels like a dream come true,” Ishika told PTI.Her father has been her coach from the start and her family has always supported her hockey journey. But injuries and difficult periods tested her mentally."My father has been my coach since the beginning. So I have always had great support from my family but I would say the challenge was to become mentally stronger. Injury and tough times have made me believe in myself a little more and taught me to be resilient and optimistic,” said the 21-year old.Ishika now wants to repay that support by using her pressing skills and ability to create scoring chances.For 21-year-old defender Lalthantluangi, receiving her India cap was a special moment.“Words cannot express how I feel right now. This cap is not just mine, it belongs to my family as well. The real work starts now, and I want to give my hundred percent for the country,” she said.Growing up, she had to manage school along with hockey training. That experience helped her learn how to balance different responsibilities.“Our seniors are amazing. They have taken me under their wing, taught me how to handle the pressure and they just lead by example every single day,” she said.At the World Cup, Lalthantluangi will have an important role in keeping India's defence organised and helping the team build attacks from the back.Nineteen-year-old midfielder Sakshi will enter her first World Cup with both excitement and some nerves.“There is definitely some excitement and a little nervousness because it is my first World Cup. But I think that nervous energy is good. I just want to enjoy the moment, stay focused and give my best on the field,” she said.Sakshi sees herself as a link between India's defence and attack. She will look to contribute at both ends of the field.Shilpi Dabas has taken a different route to the World Cup. Her chance to join the national setup came after a long wait.“I have received a massive platform. I am both happy and nervous,” she said.Dabas said she did not get a call-up to the national camp until after the second season of the Hockey India League. That eventually gave her a chance to enter the senior setup.“The biggest challenge was that I hadn't been called up to the camp until now; I was selected only after the second season of the Hockey India League,” Dabas said.Dabas started playing hockey in Class VI. Hockey runs in her family, with her mother, father and brother all having played the sport.She believes tackling and long-ball skills are her biggest strengths and wants to use them whenever she gets her chance.The youngster also has a message for players waiting for their own breakthrough.“Don't give up, keep working hard, and you will definitely get an opportunity eventually,” she said.Sunelita Toppo will bring pace to India's attack from the wing.“Every player dreams of playing for the country, and I am fortunate to have received this opportunity,” said the 19-year old.Speed is her biggest strength, and she wants to use it to get the ball into the striking circle quickly.“Speed is my strength, and I intend to use it for the team's benefit. Since I play on the wing, I aim to pass the ball to the striker as quickly as possible so they can score,” Toppo said.Her focus is clear: make the most of her training and perform her role for the team.Toppo also believes players must stay strong during difficult periods."You will face many challenges in life... there may even be times when you feel like quitting hockey. But if you believe in yourself and keep working hard, that effort will surely pay off,” she said.The five debutants have taken different paths to reach the World Cup, but their goal is the same.They now have the chance to play on the biggest stage, learn from India's experienced players and turn years of hard work into performances for the country.
Article Summary: Ishika, Lalthantluangi, Sakshi Rana, Shilpi Dabas and Sunelita Toppo make debuts. Ishika: 'Representing India at the biggest stage is every player’s dream' Sakshi: 'I just want to enjoy the moment, stay focused and give my best on the field'

Article Title: 'More than pressure, it’s responsibility': Harmanpreet Singh on India’s World Cup medal drought
Article Text:
Indian Hockey Team (ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Back-to-back Hockey World Cups on home soil, and sixth- and ninth-place finishes in those, still rankle India’s men’s team captain Harmanpreet Singh . As India begin their campaign against Wales on Saturday, the focus is firmly on ending a 51-year medal drought at the quadrennial event.With hard lessons learnt from the FIH Pro League, Harmanpreet’s squad went through rigorous training at the SAI South Centre in Bengaluru and a team-building and personal development camp in Switzerland. The captain is now confident India can produce a better showing this time. Excerpts...How is the team mentally prepared for the World Cup?The World Cup happens once every four years and we know its value. We played the last two editions of the tournament at home, so this will be a different experience. We want to make this opportunity memorable.What is the pressure of expecting a medal after 51 years?More than pressure, it’s responsibility. It is our legacy. Whether it is the Olympics or the World Cup, the number of times we have won in the past pushes and motivates us. We are ranked seventh, which is low for us. We go into the competition as underdogs, but with the belief that we can do well as a team.Eight players are making their World Cup debut; how have you helped them deal with expectations?Everyone knows the responsibilities. From the time they started playing hockey, they have also had a dream of representing the country at the World Cup, Asian Games, and the Olympics.They know why we have come here and what our goal is, which comes with the pressure of big tournaments and high expectations. We want to give our best performance; we don’t want to put pressure on the youngsters. We want them to enjoy the game. We have worked as a team, so we want to stick to it. We want to give our best according to our responsibilities. The result will definitely be in our favour.How has the emergence of other drag flickers helped ease the pressure on you?Even now, there is pressure, but the advantage we have is that we have more options. They have their own style and rhythm and are doing well.As the leader of the pack, what have your conversations been with them?I know a lot of things are going on in their minds. So, I’ve been talking to them about a lot of things. For instance, if we suddenly get a penalty corner after a lot of sprints, what is the best way to control their minds and calm their nerves? The message is also simple: Focus on your target. Don’t overthink. When the opportunities come your way, believe in yourself and try to give your 100%, so that you get a good finish.You’ve played England and Pakistan in the Pro League recently and will play them again in the league...We made a lot of changes in Pro League matches against both teams and did well. We carry forward that confidence from those matches. Also, their playing style is similar to ours. We have observed a lot of things and also learnt from those matches, which we will try and apply in the World Cup.What is the pressure of playing against Pakistan in the World Cup?I don’t think there is any pressure. That said, the match against Pakistan definitely has a different atmosphere. A lot of emotions are involved. But we know that our responsibility comes first, and we will focus more on that.
Article Summary: India begin their campaign against Wales on Saturday. The focus is firmly on ending a 51-year medal drought at the quadrennial event. Captain Harmanpreet Singh is confident India can produce a better showing this time. India are ranked seventh, which is low for them.

Article Title: India's 11 World Cup debutants: Deepika, Shilpi's remarkable journeys to Hockey's biggest stage
Article Text:

WC debutants:

When the Indian women’s team opens its World Cup campaign against China on Sunday, 11 players in the squad will be making their World Cup debuts. They come from different corners of the country — Mizoram, Jharkhand, Odisha, Haryana, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Punjab — and have taken different paths to reach hockey’s biggest stage.Some grew up with the sport, others took it up after playing different sports, while for some, hockey became a route to a better life. One of them is Jharkhand’s Deepika Soreng, who grew up in Simdega district and was introduced to hockey by Father Benedict Kujur at RC Upgraded Middle School in Karangaguri, where students were required to bring a hockey stick to school.Life, however, was far from certain. Deepika’s father died when she was a child, leaving her mother, Friska, to take up whatever work she could to support her daughter and two sons.“When I later got a chance to join the residential academy in Simdega, my mother went to Rourkela to work at the steel plant,” said Deepika, one of three students of late coach Pratima Barwa — alongside Salima Tete and Beauty Dungdung — who will play at the World Cup.Friska spent more than a decade working at the steel plant, living away from her children so they could continue their education and pursue their dreams. Years later, after Deepika broke into the national team and secured a job with the Railways, she was finally able to bring her mother back home.Friska now lives in Ranchi in her daughter’s apartment. “Next, I would like to take my mother somewhere by air. She has never travelled by flight, and I really want her to experience that at least once,” Deepika said.Because of the circumstances, Friska has not been able to follow her daughter’s hockey journey closely. She knows Deepika plays hockey and represents India, but herself knows little about the game itself. In another corner of the country, Anita Dabas, however, has closely followed her daughter Shilpi’s every step as she tried to break into the national team. A former national player from Haryana who also represented Air India, Anita made it to the India camp around 30 years ago.“She couldn’t make the team eventually. But now Shilpi has got that opportunity to represent India at the World Cup and it feels like the dream of the entire family has come true,” Shilpi’s father Anil, told TOI from their home in Sonipat. For Shilpi, the wait has been agonising. She has been playing senior nationals since 2018, but it was only earlier this year that she finally received a call-up to the senior national camp following her performance in Women’s Hockey India League with SG Pipers.“I had been trying for many years. Whenever there was a national selection or tournament, I would think, ‘Maybe my name will come this time.’ I would feel that surely it would happen now, but it just wasn’t happening,” the 28-year-old told TOI from Netherlands. There were moments of frustration, but Shilpi never stopped working. Her parents and coach Pritam Siwach ensured she kept going through the difficult years.“She would get irritated and frustrated at times. There were many occasions when I had to motivate her,” said Pritam.The persistence has now paid off. Shilpi has not only sealed her place in the World Cup squad but also played a major role in India’s Nations Cup triumph in June. Anil credits the Haryana state association and her first coach, Rajinder Singh Sr., a member of India’s 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal-winning squad, for playing important roles in her development. Pratima did much the same for Deepika, guiding her for almost a decade before her death last year. Deepika, however, will carry her coach’s memory when she takes the field on Sunday, as will Salima and Beauty.And while they will share the same World Cup stage, the journeys that brought Deepika and Shilpi there could hardly have been more different. They were on two very different paths leading to the same dream.Lalthantluangi, Shilpi Dabas, Ishika Chaudhary, Sakshi Rana, Sunelita Toppo, Deepika Soreng, DeepikaRutuja Dadaso Pisal, Ishika, Baljeet Kaur, Beauty Dungdung
Article Summary: 11 players in the squad will be making their World Cup debuts. They come from different corners of the country. Some grew up with the sport, others took it up after playing different sports. For some, hockey became a route to a better life. Deepika Soreng's father died when she was a child.

Article Title: Jammu & Kashmir set to host Irani Cup at Srinagar's Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium after four decades
Article Text:

Mumbai: In what would be the biggest cricket match in Jammu & Kashmir since the 1980s, the Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium in Srinagar is gearing up to host the Irani Cup match in October this year between 2025-26 Ranji Trophy winners Jammu and Kashmir and the Rest of India from October 1 to 5.This will be the biggest cricket match to be held in Kashmir since the ODI between India and Australia on September 9, 1986. The venue has hosted two ODIs. In the first match there, India played the West Indies on October 13, 1983, with the visitors being declared the winners in a weather-affected game. In the second match, Australia defeated India by three wickets.From October 15-18 last year, the Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium hosted a key Ranji Trophy match between Mumbai and J&K. Left-arm spinning all-rounder Shams Mulani won the 'Player of the Match' award after scoring 91 in the first innings and taking seven for 46 in the second innings."The Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium in Srinagar will host the Irani Cup match between J&K and RoI from Oct 1-5," Jammu & Kashmir head coach Ajay Sharma told TOI."The stadium is bracing for the big game. It will need a major uplift as the match will be telecast live. The BCCI has sent its team twice to Srinagar to guide the Jammu & Kashmir Cricket Association on what needs to be done to host the big game. We need to have a commentators' box, proper telecast arrangements, a media box and a few more stands - both temporary and permanent - for the spectators," a source tracking developments told TOI on Wednesday.Presently, the stadium's seating capacity is 5,000 spectators.The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is yet to officially confirm the venue for the Irani Cup 2026.Captained by 41-year-old batter Paras Dogra, Jammu & Kashmir will obviously bank on swing bowler Auqib Nabi Dar, who was recently picked for India's two-Test tour of Sri Lanka. The 29-year-old fast bowler from Baramulla picked up 60 wickets at 12.56 in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy to finish as the leading wicket-taker.The Rest of India have won 30 Irani Cup titles so far, followed by Mumbai with 15 titles.After playing the Irani Cup tie, J&K will launch their Ranji Trophy title defence on October 11 against Madhya Pradesh. The defending champions are placed in Elite Group A in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy, along with Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Baroda, Puducherry, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Goa.
Article Summary: The Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium in Srinagar is gearing up to host the Irani Cup match between 2025-26 Ranji Trophy winners Jammu and Kashmir and the Rest of India from October 1 to 5. This will be the biggest cricket match to be held in Kashmir since the ODI between India and Australia on September 9, 1986. The venue has hosted two ODIs.

Article Title: World Cup victory fuels India's hunger, Jemimah Rodrigues sets sights on Champions Trophy 2027

India face South Africa test before Champions Trophy

Indian batter Jemimah Rodrigues believes the inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy will be a special occasion for the team, with India's recent World Cup triumph in 2025 only making the squad more determined to replicate its success on the global stage. Rodrigues, who is currently recovering from a hamstring injury suffered during her stint with Southern Brave in The Hundred 2026, spoke about India's ambitions during an interaction on JioHotstar's Follow the Blues.India's historic World Cup triumph has given the team a taste of success, and Rodrigues believes that experience has only strengthened their desire to remain at the top."We've tasted success once, and we know what it feels like to be at the top. The more you taste it, the more you want to be there," Rodrigues said JioStar.The inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy is scheduled to be held in Sri Lanka from February 14 to 28, 2027. It will mark the first edition of the Champions Trophy in women's international cricket. Rodrigues is particularly excited about being part of the tournament's inaugural edition and believes India's recent success will provide additional motivation."Our team is working towards that, and yes, the Champions Trophy is going to be very special. It's happening for the first time ever in women's cricket, and I'll be a part of it for the first time as well, so it'll be pretty special, and I'm really looking forward to it," she added.The tournament was initially scheduled for a June-July window but was subsequently moved to early 2027 following an ICC board decision. The women's Champions Trophy will feature six teams competing in the T20I format. The tournament will consist of a round-robin league stage, with the top two teams progressing to the final. A total of 16 matches will be played across the competition.Before turning their attention fully towards the Champions Trophy, India will face South Africa in a challenging multi-format tour beginning on December 9, 2026. The series will see the two recent World Cup finalists renew their rivalry across formats, with India scheduled to play a one-off Test, three ODIs and three T20Is.

Former Union minister and former MP Meenakshi Lekhi has been appointed chairperson of the Divyang Cricket Control Board of India (DCCBI), the organisation overseeing the Indian Divyang Cricket Team and Indian Wheelchair Cricket Team.The announcement was made during a Divyang Cricket Award ceremony in Agra, where Lekhi was formally entrusted with the responsibility. Addressing players, officials and organisers, she said she would discharge the role with dedication and work towards taking divyang cricket to new heights at both the national and international levels.Lekhi urged players to draw inspiration from the life of Lord Ram, highlighting the importance of duty, perseverance and integrity. According to Lekhi, the responsibility towards players with disabilities extends beyond the sporting arena, with society needing to ensure that they receive respect, opportunities and better prospects for the future.DCCBI president Mukesh Kanchan welcomed Lekhi's appointment, saying the board needed a leader who could motivate players to work hard, overcome challenges and focus on their goals. He expressed confidence that her guidance would help divyang cricket reach new heights.Dr Bhagwan Talware, president of the Wheelchair Unit, said Lekhi's experience, leadership abilities and social commitment would provide a new direction and greater strength to divyang cricket.The board is also seeking to expand international opportunities. It is working towards organising a triangular divyang cricket series involving India, Sri Lanka and Nepal in Mumbai. NEW DELHI: For Kuldeep Yadav , India's two-Test series against Sri Lanka is an important opportunity. With the team going through a transition, Kuldeep can strengthen his case to become a key part of India's red-ball plans. Ravindra Jadeja is in the twilight of his career, and India need to identify their next generation of spinners. Kuldeep's experience could make him an important part of that transition.Former India spinner Murali Kartik believes Kuldeep has a chance to play a bigger role.However, Kuldeep's numbers under different captains show that he remained an important bowler across formats.Under Rohit, Kuldeep played 62 matches and took 116 wickets at an average of 20.92. He took four five-wicket hauls, with his best figures being 6/25.Under Shubman Gill, Kuldeep has played nine matches and taken 23 wickets at an average of 27.65. His best figures are 5/82.The numbers underline the different roles Kuldeep has had under India's captains."And look, Kuldeep Yadav has been a match-winner for India, but unfortunately for him, things played out differently when he had Rohit Sharma and Rahul Dravid as the captain and coach, respectively, and now he has not got that kind of run in the side. When you think of what happened in England, everybody kept saying during the course of those five Test matches, 'Where is Kuldeep? Where is Kuldeep?' And Kuldeep didn't play; he was sitting out. So it's very important from that point of view. Now that Ravindra Jadeja is in the twilight of his career, is he the leader, or is it going to be someone else? Because it is, as you rightly said, very, very difficult," he said.Kuldeep has played 18 Tests for India and taken 79 wickets in 34 innings. He has a bowling average of 22.35, an economy rate of 3.53 and a strike rate of 37.9. He has taken four four-wicket hauls and five five-wicket hauls.His best innings figures are 5/40, while his best match figures are 8/113.Kuldeep has also been a successful limited-overs bowler. He has 194 wickets from 121 ODIs at an average of 27.04. In 54 T20Is, he has taken 95 wickets at an average of 13.74.With Jadeja nearing the twilight of his career, Kartik believes India's spin attack is entering an important phase."From a spin point of view, it is absolutely important because Ravindra Jadeja, as good as he has been for Indian cricket, is in the twilight of his career. So, from that point of view, Manav Suthar, the way he came in and the way he bowled against Afghanistan, was very heartwarming for any old-school spinner who has watched Indian cricket or knows Indian cricket. So, from that point of view, from a red-ball perspective, Manav Suthar is very important," Kartik said.Suthar has already given India reason to be hopeful. He took seven wickets on his Test debut against Afghanistan in June. Suthar is another option for India, but Kuldeep brings greater experience and has already shown that he can win matches with the ball.The series also comes at an important time in India's World Test Championship campaign.India are currently fifth in the WTC standings. They have won four and lost four of their nine matches, with one draw. Their points percentage is 48.15.Kartik believes India need to improve their recent Test record."It is a crucial tour, very important not just from the point of view of the spinners alone but also the WTC, because if we are serious about Test cricket, we are at No. 5. Our fortunes haven't been great in red-ball cricket of late, which is well documented and everyone knows it," he said.
Article Summary: Kuldeep Yadav has played 18 Tests for India and taken 79 wickets in 34 innings. Ravindra Jadeja is in the twilight of his career, and India need to identify their next generation of spinners. Former India spinner Murali Kartik believes Kuldeep has a chance to play a bigger role.

Article Title: Pakistan players 'more focused on earning money': Former chief selector makes huge claim
Article Text:
Pakistan crowd during a cricket match

Qasim questions players’ priorities

Lessons from the past

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan Test spinner and ex-chief selector Iqbal Qasim has criticised the current generation of cricketers, saying too many young players are more focused on earning money than improving their skills and understanding of the game.Qasim, who played 50 Tests and served on the national selection committee several times, also questioned the lack of long-term planning and consistency in selection decisions.“I have been a chief selector and member of the selection committee several times and we worked on an honorary basis with no salaries or fees,” he recalled, as quoted by PTI.“Nowadays the selectors get paid handsome salaries for being on the selection committee but I see a lack of vision when making decisions,” he said.The former spinner, who finished his first-class career with 999 wickets, believes Pakistan cricket is being affected by a lack of commitment among young players.“I don’t want to talk about the past or when we played cricket. But seriously I see a general lack of interest or commitment among most of the young players to focus and work hard on improving their game awareness and skills and they seem more focused on earning money,” he said.Qasim said players now have greater financial opportunities, but many youngsters consider success to be mainly about securing Pakistan Super League contracts.“Even now with cricket changing so much over the last few decades the formula to success remains that how much time is a player (s) individually willing to give to improve upon his skill sets and reading the game. And that is not happening frequently now in Pakistan cricket.”“There is too much reliance on young players on coaches, assistants and data; they don’t spend enough time individually on working out things.”He said the best players have always worked independently on their skills, fitness and ability to understand match situations.“I think playing for your country is the biggest reward a player can get. I have always believed the better you improve your quality as a player the more money will come automatically you don’t have to chase it,” he added.Qasim also recalled Pakistan’s famous Test win over India in Bangalore in 1987, where advice from former India captain Bishen Singh Bedi helped shape his approach.“We met Bishen Sahab at a function on the rest day of the Bangalore test and he was unhappy with his prodigy Maninder Singh’s bowling in the second innings noting on a pitch where there was so much turn he (Maninder) was giving so much turn to the ball that it was impossible to bowl a batsman, get leg before or trap him into giving a catch.”Qasim said he followed Bedi’s advice to bowl in the right areas and use the pitch’s natural turn, helping Pakistan win the match.He also recalled refusing to exclude Shahid Afridi from a West Indies tour despite opposition from captain Misbah-ul-Haq.“I told Zaka Sahab and captain, Misbah who didn’t want Afridi in the team that it is the selectors' domain to pick 16 best players and it is the captain's domain to play the 11 he wanted. So I would not drop Afridi. Misbah told me he will not play him and I said fine that is your prerogative but he will go,” he recalled.Afridi eventually played and took several wickets in his first match. Qasim believes interference between different authorities remains a major problem for Pakistan cricket, creating confusion and controversy.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan spinner Iqbal Qasim has criticised the current generation of cricketers. He says too many young players are more focused on earning money than improving their skills and understanding of the game. The former spinner also questioned the lack of long-term planning and consistency in selection decisions.

England captain Joe Root has said there will be no team curfew during next week's three-Test series against Pakistan, saying players should be trusted to make responsible decisions away from the field.Root, 35, spoke as England's dressing-room culture continues to face scrutiny following a series of off-field incidents over the past year during the tenure of former coach Brendon McCullum and former captain Ben Stokes Root returned as England's Test captain after Stokes retired during the Test series against New Zealand in June. Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson were suspended for one Test after breaking a team curfew during a night out in London.McCullum stepped down after England lost the series 2-1 and was replaced by former New Zealand teammate Stephen Fleming.Despite the previous incidents, Root said England would not introduce a curfew for the Pakistan series."There’s not going to be a curfew. I don’t think this needs to be a big deal, to be honest," Root said on the Sky Sports Cricket podcast published on Wednesday.He said players should be trusted to take responsibility for their actions away from cricket as they are expected to do on the field."My view is that if players are expected to take responsibility on the field, they should be trusted as grown adults to make good decisions off it as well.""That’s something we, as a team, have to manage properly and police ourselves, alongside Stephen Fleming."England's team culture has been under scrutiny since their 4-1 Ashes defeat in Australia last year, with several off-field incidents adding to the debate.One of those incidents involved England batter Harry Brook and a nightclub bouncer in New Zealand.ECB chief executive Richard Gould had said in January that England players would face stricter measures, including a midnight curfew.England currently sit seventh in the World Test Championship standings.Root and Fleming will begin their time together with the three-Test series against Pakistan, with the first Test scheduled to start on August 19.
Article Summary: England captain Joe Root says there will be no team curfew during next week's three-Test series against Pakistan. Root says players should be trusted to make responsible decisions away from the field. England's team culture has been under scrutiny since their 4-1 Ashes defeat in Australia last year.

Article Title: English all-rounder Danny Lamb forced to retire from cricket aged 30 after neck, spinal cord injury
Article Text:
Danny Lamb

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sussex all-rounder Danny Lamb has retired from professional cricket at the age of 30 after an injury to his neck and spinal cord forced him to end his career.Lamb suffered a disc herniation in his neck earlier this season, which led to a spinal cord injury. He underwent surgery last month but continued to deal with the effects of the injury. After taking medical advice, the right-arm bowler decided to retire for the sake of his long-term health."It is incredibly difficult to have my career end through injury," Lamb said, as quoted by Sussex."After taking medical advice I know it is the right decision for my long-term health. It has been a privilege to spend over a decade in the professional game, and I am extremely grateful to have represented both Lancashire and Sussex.""I was never the most naturally gifted player, but I always tried to give everything for the team and do whatever was required to help us win, and I have been fortunate to experience some incredible moments that will stay with me forever."Lamb's retirement comes a week after England fast bowler John Turner announced his retirement at 25 because of injury problems. Turner, who played four internationals for England in 2024, still had two years remaining on his Hampshire contract and also held an ECB development contract until late last year.Lamb played 93 matches for Lancashire across formats before joining Sussex in 2023. His career included a highest first-class score of 134 and eight first-class wickets at an average of 33.13.He has not played for Sussex since early June because of the injury. His last appearance came in the Vitality Blast against Kent, when Sussex recorded their only home win of the campaign.Sussex head coach and director of cricket Paul Farbrace thanked Lamb for his contribution to the club."It is always a sad day when any professional athlete has to retire from the sport they love; it's even harder when it is because of injury."Danny [Lamb] sadly is not able to continue his career and I would like to thank him for his high level of commitment and skill that he has dedicated to his time at Hove."Danny played a leading role in our promotion to Division One in the County Championship and us getting to Finals Day in the Blast."
Article Summary: Sussex all-rounder Danny Lamb has retired from professional cricket at the age of 30. Lamb suffered a disc herniation in his neck earlier this season, which led to a spinal cord injury. The right-arm bowler decided to retire for the sake of his long-term health.

Article Title: Hours after Gautam Gambhir's visit to Galle, lawn mower hits the pitch
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir's visit to Galle (Photo by PTI and TimesofIndia.com)

TimesofIndia.com in Galle:

Galle Stadium (Photo by TimesofIndia.com)

Sri Lanka held a closed-door practice session on Wednesday. Although the facility remained off-limits to the public and the media, the iconic Galle Fort offered a brilliant view of the proceedings. Midway through their hit, the hosts got a surprise visitor as India head coach Gautam Gambhir and batting coach Sitanshu Kotak dropped in to take a look at the pitch. The cover briefly came off for the duo and was immediately put back on the moment they left. In the practice nets adjacent to the playing surface, Sri Lanka continued to train while the groundstaff applied finishing touches.Less than two hours after Gambhir and Kotak left, the main cover came off and a grass mower was out on the playing surface. Under close watch, the groundstaff made plenty of trips up and down the 22 yards before vacating for the soft roller to do its magic. It was exposed to the sun for a while before the covers were again put on.The pitch will attract considerable attention as it is set to heavily influence India's playing XI combination.Three days before the Test and it looks like options for both three seamers and three spinners are very much on the table. The management had emphasised in the past that they need to factor in Day 1 before finalising the bowling combination. So if the pitch doesn't scream turn, it wouldn't be a susprise if Mohammed Siraj , Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar play.The selection puzzle isn't that difficult for the visitors to solve, but the crucial call between an extra seamer or spinner could well be the deal clincher. With no luxury of a Washington Sundar or a seam-bowling all-rounder like Nitish Kumar Reddy, the side can't afford to get their specialists wrong.The match-up logic could well keep Saransh Jain in the conversation, but Kuldeep Yadav must play the two Tests to give captain Shubman Gill the best shot at picking 20 wickets, in the absence of an injured Jasprit Bumrah.Apart from the playing XI, the weather apps will also keep the Indian management busy, as there have been short-but-very-strong spells of rain since the team checked into their sea-facing resort. It was clearer and sunnier on Wednesday but there is a strong forecast of rain in the coming week.India didn't train on August 11 and 12 but will hit the ground starting at 10am on Thursday. The team had an intense workout in Colombo, featuring three high-intensity training sessions and a three-day warm-up where all batters and bowlers got a good feel in the middle.The match simulation on the final day at the NCC Ground concluded a fruitful week for Gill & Co. and they would hit Galle refreshed and rejuvenated for the business end of preps.

Rocky Flintoff scored his first senior professional century as Lancashire beat Somerset by 174 runs in the One-Day Cup and secured a place in the quarter-finals.The 18-year-old, son of former England all-rounder Andrew Flintoff, made 123 off 76 balls, hitting 10 fours and seven sixes. He has to go out there and do it himself and there is every sign he is going to do just that."He has a fantastic physique for a cricketer and a good head on young shoulders. Today he used his feet well and played a fantastic knock."Flintoff's century came as part of a record-breaking team performance from Lancashire, who crossed 400 for the first time in their List A history with their total of 443.Rocky has already represented England at youth and second-string level, having played for both the England Lions and England Under-19s. His latest innings was his first century in senior professional cricket.

Article Title: Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood, Lyon reunite as Australia begin 20-Test marathon season with Bangladesh series
Article Text:
Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon, Mitchell Starc, and Pat Cummins

Australia's batting questions

Bangladesh without key bowlers

A busy year ahead

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Test cricket returns to Australia's tropical Top End for the first time since 2003 when the hosts take on Bangladesh in a two-match series beginning Thursday.The first Test at Marrara Stadium in Darwin will be Bangladesh's first Test tour of Australia in more than 20 years. It also starts a 12-month period in which Australia are scheduled to play at least 20 Tests, including series against South Africa, India and England.Australia are set to bring back their main bowling attack, with Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon returning from injuries. Mitchell Starc is also in the side.Injuries have meant the four have rarely played together in recent series. Hazlewood's expected return means Scott Boland will miss out, while allrounders Cameron Green and Beau Webster are also in the starting XI.“We know Scotty's class, it is always a pretty tight call,” Cummins said at a press conference on Wednesday. “There is not much you can say to Scotty except there is a lot of cricket coming up.“He knows his worth, and how good he is, and I am sure he will be out there at some point pretty soon.”Australia's bowling attack looks settled, but there are questions over the batting order.Jake Weatherald, the first Test player from Australia's Northern Territory, has kept his place after Australia's Ashes win over England last season despite his recent form.He is expected to open with Travis Head.Usman Khawaja's retirement has allowed Australia to play both Green and Webster in the same XI. Marnus Labuschagne and Steve Smith will bat at No. 3 and No. 4, with Labuschagne also looking for runs to strengthen his position in the side.Bangladesh will be without Nahid Rana, Mustafizur Rahman and Shoriful Islam for the first Test. Shoriful could return for the second match in Mackay from August 22 to 26.Rana, 23, is one of Bangladesh's quickest bowlers and was a key part of their ODI series win over Australia two months ago. He suffered a side strain during a T20I against Zimbabwe in July.The series against Bangladesh begins a schedule of 20 Tests for Australia over the next 12 months, with another match possible if they qualify for the World Test Championship final.After the second Bangladesh Test, Australia will tour South Africa for three Tests in October. They will then host New Zealand for four Tests before a five-Test series in India.Australia will also play a one-off day-night Test against England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in March to mark the 150th anniversary of matches between the two countries.The schedule will conclude with an away Ashes series beginning in June.
Article Summary: Australia set to bring back their main bowling attack, with Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon returning from injuries. Mitchell Starc is also in the side. The first Test at Marrara Stadium in Darwin will be Bangladesh's first Test tour of Australia in more than 20 years.

NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the women’s -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest. The state government also presented her with a cheque of Rs 10 lakh as part of the felicitation.Speaking at the event, Saha highlighted Dey’s difficult journey from a small village in South Tripura to the top of the Commonwealth Games podium. Her father, he noted, worked as a cycle mechanic in Sonaichari.“The journey from an obscure village in South Tripura to a podium finish at Glasgow was a race against time. Her father was a cycle mechanic at Sonaichari. Against all odds, she stood firm on her mission and achieved phenomenal success for the country,” he said.The chief minister recalled meeting Dey at Tripura Bhavan in New Delhi after her return from the Games.During that meeting, the judoka had expressed her wish to have a house in Agartala.“During the meeting, Asmita revealed she desperately wanted a house in Agartala.
